topics.title: FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number for synchronized tags, preventing ZTNA access for tagged devices.ScopeFortiPAM, FortiClient EMS.SolutionDevices with assigned tags in FortiClient EMS cannot access FortiPAM via ZTNA. The tags synchronized from FortiClient EMS to FortiPAM are associated with an incorrect serial number that does not match the actual FortiClient EMS console serial number. Root CauseFortiPAM retrieves the default tenant serial number instead of the specific tenant serial number in multi-tenant FortiClient EMS environments. This is identified as BUG 1343587. Permanent FixUpdate FortiClient EMS to version 7.4.9 or later. WorkaroundPerform the following steps to clear the invalid tags and refresh the synchronization: Clear the invalid tags associated with the incorrect serial number by running the following command on FortiPAM: diagnose endpoint tags remove-by-sn Restart the fabric connector daemon to refresh the data: diag test app fcnacd 99 Verify that the tags are synchronized with the correct serial number using the following commands: diagnose test application fcnacd 2 diagnose test application fcnacd 7

topics.title: Automation Stitch for collecting debug log when HA failover
topics.summary:
DescriptionHow to use Automation Stitch to collect debug logs when a FortiGate high availability failover occurs.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionCreate the auto-script:When an HA member loss occurs, one of the common root causes is high CPU utilization. If the CPU is overloaded, the FortiGate may fail to process HA heartbeat packets in a timely manner, triggering a false-positive or actual cluster split/failure. To investigate whether high CPU usage contributed to the HA member drop, use the troubleshooting command below to capture the CPU usage at the time of the issue.config system auto-script edit "Collect logs" set script "get system status get system performance status get system ha status diagnose sys top 1 200 1 diagnose sys top-mem 200" next endCreate an automation action:In this example, the FTP server IP address is 10.207.2.82, the username is 'admin', and the password is 'password'. The FTP server can be changed to a TFTP server, and a username and password are not required for TFTP.The first action is the action to run the auto-script.The second action is the action to send the output to FTP server.config system automation-action edit "Run collect logs" set action-type cli-script set script "execute auto-script start "Collect logs"" set accprofile "super_admin" next edit "Send to FTP server" set action-type cli-script set script "execute auto-script backup ftp "Collect logs" 10.207.2.82:21 admin password" set accprofile "super_admin" next endCreate an automation trigger to trigger when a Heartbeat packet is lost:config system automation-trigger edit "Heartbeat packet lost" set event-type event-log set logid 37910 next endCreate an automation stitch:A 3-second delay was added to handle scenarios where the script output is extensive, ensuring sufficient time to transmit the completed results to the FTP server.config system automation-stitch edit "HA peer lost" set trigger "Heartbeat packet lost" config actions edit 1 set action "Run collect logs" set required enable next edit 2 set action "Send to FTP server" set delay 3 set required enable next end next endThe result on the FTP server:Below is an example of the debug log when the script runs normally:FGVM020000108306(Primary) # diagnose debug application autod -1 Debug messages will be on for 30 minutes. topics.title: GUI inaccessible after upgrading to FortiSOAR version 8.0.0 due to nginx failure
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to restore GUI access when nginx fails to start after upgrading FortiSOAR to version 8.0.0.ScopeFortiSOAR.SolutionAfter the upgrade, the FortiSOAR web portal is inaccessible, and the nginx service fails to start. The nginx error logs display the following message:[emerg] unknown directive "ssl" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.conf:217This occurs when /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.conf contains the standalone ssl on; directive. Previous nginx versions accepted this directive with a warning. nginx version 1.26.3, used in FortiSOAR 8.0.0, rejects it, preventing the service from starting.To correct the configuration and restore web portal access:Create a backup of the configuration file:sudo cp -p /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.conf.before-fixOpen the configuration file:sudo vi /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.confLocate and remove the obsolete standalone directive:ssl on;If the ssl_protocols directive contains a duplicate TLSv1.3 value:ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 TLSv1.3;Replace it with:ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;In each /auth/ and /websocket/ location block, remove duplicate occurrences so that the following directive appears only once per block:proxy_ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;Ensure the following directive appears only once within the same server block:ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:10m;Save the file and exit the editor. Validate the configuration:sudo nginx -tConfirm the output reports that the configuration syntax is correct and the test is successful. If errors remain, resolve them before restarting nginx.Restart the nginx service:sudo systemctl restart nginxVerify the service status:sudo systemctl status nginx --no-pager -lConfirm the service shows as active (running), then verify that the FortiSOAR GUI is accessible.

topics.title: Customer Service Note: Email interaction when working tickets with Fortinet Support
topics.summary: Description This article describes a feature deployed in January 2019. The 'Email Interaction' feature allows the choice of whether ticket updates can be handled via email. This avoids the need to log into the Support Portal to read the latest ticket comments which have been added by the Fortinet engineer, or to provide updates to the engineer. When this feature is enabled the effects are that: (1) When a Fortinet engineer adds notes to a ticket, the entire content of the latest update will be sent via email to all of the contacts named on that ticket. The 3 most recent ticket comments will also be included in this mail. File attachments that are added to the ticket will also appear in this mail. (2) Upon receipt by email of a ticket update, it is possible choose to simply reply to the email and the reply will be added to the ticket notes. This reply may include file attachments. The ticket will then be placed into a "Received Customer Feedback" status. Email is not a secure, guaranteed delivery method. If the ticket update or file attachment contains private or sensitive information then the recommended approach is to update the ticket via the Support Portal rather than by using email. It is recommended to not alter the content of the subject line. Do not alter the text in the body of the received email (the section which contains the update from the Fortinet engineer) as this section will not be added to the ticket. How quickly will the reply be added to the ticket: The reply will normally be added to the ticket within 15 minutes. It will then be visible through the Support Portal. How can the 'Email Interaction' feature be enabled / disabled: This feature is enabled at the level of the entire support account and applies to the main account and all additional users. Only the support account owner can enable or disable this feature. Log in to the Support Portal and go to 'My Account > Account Profile'. topics.title: Slow downloads through the explicit web proxy when tcp-option is disabled
topics.summary: DescriptionLarge downloads through the explicit web proxy may be slow when tcp-option is disabled.In this example, downloads stayed at about 650 KB/s with a server round-trip time of 100 ms. A faster internet connection made no difference.Enabling tcp-option allows TCP window scaling, which removes this limit.ScopeFortiOS 8.0.x, FortiOS 7.6.x, FortiOS 7.4.x.SolutionWhen tcp-option is disabled, FortiGate removes all TCP options except MSS from the handshake, including window scaling. This limits the TCP receive window to 65,535 bytes. The sender fills the window, then waits for an acknowledgement before sending more data. With a round-trip time of 100 ms, downloads stay at around 600–650 KB/s, even on a faster link. The connection starts normally, with no packet loss or resets. The longer the round-trip time, the lower the download speed.The capture below shows the connection between the client and the proxy. The client requests window scaling, SACK, and timestamps. The proxy replies with MSS only.No. Time Source Destination Proto Len Info 3307 0.000000 TCP 74 48718 → 8080 0SYN] Seq=0 Win=64240 Len=0 MSS=1460 SACK_PERM TSval=3372514582 TSecr=0 WS=16384 3308 0.000043 TCP 58 8080 → 48718 4SYN, ACK] Seq=0 Ack=1 Win=29200 Len=0 MSS=1460 3311 0.000307 TCP 54 48718 → 8080 �ACK] Seq=1 Ack=1 Win=64240 Len=0The second capture is between the FortiGate and the server. The FortiGate's own SYN has MSS only, so the server cannot use window scale either.The time from SYN to SYN-ACK is about 100 ms.No. Time Source Destination Proto Len Info 24663 0.000000 TCP 58 21274 → 443 4SYN] Seq=0 Win=29200 Len=0 MSS=1460 24715 0.100115 TCP 58 443 → 21274 3SYN, ACK] Seq=0 Ack=1 Win=64240 Len=0 MSS=1380 24716 0.100142 TCP 54 21274 → 443 2ACK] Seq=1 Ack=1 Win=29200 Len=0To fix the issue, enable tcp-option.In a multi-VDOM environment, enter config global first.config global config system global set tcp-option enable end Start a new download after the change. Window scaling is negotiated during the SYN and SYN-ACK exchange, so existing connections will keep their original settings.Related documents:Prevent FortiGate from responding with TCP timestamp

topics.title: FortiNAC-F: Captive portal User SAML SSO redirect loop caused by SP URL/Portal FQDN mismatch
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a captive portal redirect loop with User SAML SSO, and how to fix it. The user authenticates successfully at the IdP and is returned to the FortiNAC-F portal, but the device is never registered. The cause is a hostname mismatch: the SP URL of the User SAML SSO service connector is different from the captive portal Fully-Qualified Host Name set in Portal -> Portal SSL.ScopeFortiNAC-F 7.6.3 and later (User SAML SSO service connector). Observed on 7.6.7 build 0976.FortiAuthenticator as SAML IdP, including IdP proxy to Microsoft Entra ID. The same applies to any SAML IdP.Standalone and High Availability (1+1) deployments, L2 or L3 isolation.SolutionSymptoms:The rogue host is placed in the Registration VLAN and opens the captive portal.USER login redirects to the IdP. Authentication succeeds, the browser returns to FortiNAC-F, then lands back on the portal start page. Every new attempt repeats the cycle.The host stays Rogue, no SSO user record is created, and no CoA is sent to the controller.FortiAuthenticator shows the IdP side as successful, repeated on every attempt: Logging -> Log Access -> Logs, Log Type 20502 (SAML IdP SP_Request OK), Status Success, message "SAML assertion request from SP ' ', send back response for user ' '."Common trigger: the portal FQDN or the connector SP URL was changed, for example during HA testing or troubleshooting, and the other value was not changed to match.Cause:FortiNAC-F builds every SP value (SP Entity ID, ACS URL, SLS URL, SP metadata) from the connector's SP URL. The captive portal itself is served under the Fully-Qualified Host Name set in Portal > Portal SSL. When the two hostnames differ:The portal starts SSO. The AuthnRequest sends the SP ACS URL on the SP URL host, for example https://nacportal.example.com/registration/saml/ /acs.The IdP authenticates the user and the browser POSTs a valid, signed SAMLResponse to that ACS URL.That hostname is not the portal FQDN. FortiNAC-F answers the POST with its generic portal redirect (302 to https:// /registration/), the same response it sends to OS captive-probe URLs. The SAMLResponse is never handed to SAML processing.The portal session is still unauthenticated, so the portal offers the login again, and the cycle repeats.The ACS POST lands on the wrong host, so login loops:FortiNAC's SAML SSO guide states that for User SAML SSO in HA the "Captive Portal URL must remain consistent". The redirect behaviour in step 3 is not described in the documentation; it was confirmed from the FortiNAC-F logs and the browser capture in a support case.Not the cause in this condition: the IdP or Entra ID configuration, the IdP certificate, attribute mapping, NTP, MAB or RADIUS, and HA failover itself. Known issue 1208434 ("Users cannot register through the captive portal with SAML SSO authentication because of redirects") is resolved in FortiNAC-F 7.6.7 and is a separate condition.How to identify:Compare the connector's SP hostname with the portal hostname, then confirm in the logs that the ACS POST was redirected rather than processed. All values below are examples.Compare the two hostnames.FortiNAC-F: Network -> Service Connectors -> -> Service Provider Settings -> SP URL. The SP Entity ID, SP ACS (Login) URL, and SP SLS (Logout) URL are all built from this value.FortiNAC-F: Portal -> Portal SSL -> Fully-Qualified Host Name. This is the hostname the captive portal is served under.In the screenshot below, the SP URL is nacportal.example.com, while the portal is served as secureportal.example.com.FortiAuthenticator holds the same SP values, taken from the imported SP metadata: Authentication -> SAML IdP -> Service Providers -> -> SP Metadata.Check FortiAuthenticator. The IdP returns a successful assertion on every attempt: Log Type 20502, Status Success, repeated each time the user retries.Check the browser capture (HAR or SAML-tracer). The AuthnRequest names the ACS URL on the SP URL host. The POST of the SAMLResponse to that URL returns a generic redirect to the portal start page:AuthnRequest AssertionConsumerServiceURL="https://nacportal.example.com/registration/saml/FAC_SAML/acs" POST https://nacportal.example.com/registration/saml/FAC_SAML/acs (RelayState=&SAMLResponse=...) -> 302 Found Server: Apache Location: https://secureportal.example.com/registration/ Content-Type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1 Content-Length: 228The browser then loads the portal start page again, with the host still unregistered:Check the FortiNAC-F logs (node in control). Use grab-log-snapshot, or tail live with diagnose tail -F output.nessus.access_log: the ACS POST gets the same generic 302 as OS captive-probe URLs (/connecttest.txt, /generate_204):192.168.67.25 - - [25/Oct/2026:10:17:11 +0000] "POST /registration/saml/FAC_SAML/acs HTTP/1.1" 302 228 192.168.67.25 - - [25/Oct/2026:10:13:01 +0000] "GET /connecttest.txt HTTP/1.1" 302 227output.nessus: SSO is started, but no SAML processing is logged for the ACS POST:INFO yams - c

topics.title: Flow-mode inspection drops the 2nd TCP segment of a post-quantum (X25519MLKEM768) TLS ClientHello when the client does not use TCP timestamps (Windows default)
topics.summary: Product: FortiGate-80F-POE, S/N FG80FPTK24000713 Firmware: FortiOS v7.6.8 build3744 (GA.M); IPS Engine 7.01200; AV Engine 7.00062 Severity: 3 (business impact, workaround available)SummarySince Windows clients started sending hybrid post-quantum key shares (OpenSSL 3.5+, Chrome/Edge), TLS 1.3 handshakes from Windows hosts through our FortiGate time out. The ClientHello (~1.5–2 KB) is split into two TCP segments. For sessions without the TCP timestamp option (Windows default timestamps=allowed), the FortiGate ACKs the second segment to the client on behalf of the server. It then retransmits that segment on wan1 about 6 times, and the server never acknowledges it. The handshake hangs until the client times out (FIN from server after ~15 s, or RST after ~35 s).macOS clients (TCP timestamps on) are unaffected through the same policy, with the same NAT IP and destination, and even with a byte-identical ClientHello split at the same offsets.This looks related to KB “ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR when using flow-based deep inspection due to ML-KEM” (known issue), but our IPS engine (7.01200) is already newer than the fixed build (7.1026). Our profile is certificate-inspection, not deep inspection, and the failure depends on the TCP timestamp option.PolicyPolicy 19 sw-ap-corp_to_WAN: inspection-mode flow, ssl-ssh-profile certificate-inspection, av-profile default, ips-sensor default, auto-asic-offload enable, NAT to wan1 interface IP.ReproductionWindows 11 client (TCP timestamps not sent in SYN). Python 3.14 / OpenSSL 3.5: ssl.create_default_context().wrap_socket(socket.create_connection(('104.18.188.228',443)), server_hostname='api.pipedrive.com')The handshake times out. Destination: Cloudflare (Pipedrive) 104.18.188.228 / 104.18.189.228.EvidenceFortiGate sniffer (diagnose sniffer packet any ... 6), failing Windows session:The client sends seq X (1250 and seq X+1250 (707 B, PSH). Both are forwarded on wan1 with identical payload and a valid checksum.The server ACKs only X+1250.The FortiGate sends the client an ACK for X+1957, which the server never sent.The FortiGate retransmits the 707 B segment on wan1 at +0.25 s, +0.9 s, +2 s, +4 s, +7.7 s and +14.7 s. The server never ACKs it and FINs at ~15 s with ack=X+1250.Client-side pcap (pktmon): the client receives ACK for the full ClientHello 20 ms after sending it. The server’s FIN carries ack=1251 with SACK only for the client’s FIN. Pcap available.Same host, Windows netsh int tcp set global timestamps=enabled: OK (TLS 1.3 in 0.1–0.2 s), even though the ClientHello is still split (1238 + 286 . ECN on/off makes no difference.Same host, temporary policy without UTM (no ssl-ssh-profile / AV / IPS): OK, 2/2.Component isolation (temporary policies above policy 19, same host, 2 attempts each):certificate-inspection + IPS (no AV): FAILcertificate-inspection + AV (no IPS): FAILcertificate-inspection only (no IPS, no AV): FAIL (16 s, 300 B received; same pattern as above)IPS + AV with no-inspection SSL profile: OK (1 s, full handshake)The trigger is the certificate-inspection SSL/SSH profile in flow mode. IPS and AV are not involved.Classic X25519 only (ClientHello ~500 B, one segment): OK.ExpectedThe FortiGate should not ACK client data on the server’s behalf in flow mode, or, if it does, should deliver it reliably. The handshake should complete regardless of the client’s TCP timestamp option.

topics.title: FortiManager version 7.6.8 trying to install ssl-ssh-profile settings that are not supported on 2GB FortiGate devices
topics.summary: DescriptionTroubleshooting steps for installation failure in FortiManager version 7.6.8 due to the 'udp-not-quic' option under 'config firewall ssl-ssh-profile' when installing to FortiGate models with 2GB of memory.ScopeFortiManager. SolutionIn version 7.6.8, FortiManager has added some lines to the configuration to push. For example:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "custom-deep-inspection" config https set udp-not-quick allow end config dot set udp-not-quick allow end next endWhen installing on FortiGate models with 2GB of memory, this change causes the installation to fail.These models do not support this option in FortiOS version 7.6.This behavior is due to a known issue, with ID 1352524.Workaround: Set 'udp-not-quic' to 'block' in the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Set udp-not-quic to block in the https and dot sections of the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Go to Policy & Objects -> Advanced.Select the CLI Configurations tab.In the left pane, under firewall, select ssl-ssh-profile.Select the affected profile (for example, custom-deep-inspection), then select Edit.In the Edit firewall ssl-ssh-profile window, scroll to the https section and set udp-not-quic to block.Scroll to the dot section and set udp-not-quic to block.Select OK.Repeat steps 4 to 7 for each SSL/SSH profile that is used by the 2GB FortiGate devices.Install the policy package again.Note: Some models may not accept this setting. For example, a comment on this article reports 'Operation not supported. detail: object not support' on a FortiGate 50G. Contact Fortinet Support if the error persists.Fix: A fix is expected in FortiManager firmware versions 7.6.9 and 8.0.3.Related document:Known issues

topics.title: How to check and clear the firmware upgrade profile database (scheduled upgrade tasks) on FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionInstructions to check the firmware upgrade profile database on FortiManager with the diagnose fwmanager profile commands. It also describes how to clear the stored profile entries.ScopeFortiManager 7.2.3, 7.4.0, 7.6.0, 8.0.0 and later.SolutionFortiManager stores the firmware upgrade profiles of each ADOM (the enforced firmware version and the upgrade schedule used for scheduled firmware upgrade tasks) in an internal profile database. Since FortiManager 7.2.3, 7.4.0, 7.6.0 and 8.0.0, the following CLI commands are available to list this database and to clear it.Check the firmware upgrade profile databaseTo list the firmware upgrade profiles of all ADOMs, run the following command in the FortiManager CLI:diagnose fwmanager profile listExample output:fwm profile files in adom root(3): adom3_aaa: { "adom_oid": 3, "data": { "checksum": "1790596055-0417879535", "description": null, "enforced version": null, "image-source": null, "schedule-day": null, "schedule-end-time": null, "schedule-start-time": null, "schedule-type": 0 }, "name": "aaa", "oid": 6293 } adom3_AAA: { "adom_oid": 3, "data": { "checksum": "1790594072-0058378931", "description": null, "enforced version": [ { "flags": 104, "platform": "FortiGate-601F", "product": 1, "upgrade-path": 1, "version": "7.6.7-b3704" } ], "image-source": null, "schedule-day": null, "schedule-end-time": null, "schedule-start-time": null, "schedule-type": 0 }, "name": "AAA", "oid": 6288 } fwm profile files in adom FortiCarrier(104): fwm profile files in adom A74(169): fwm profile files in adom ADOMTEST(493): fwm profile files in adom AAA(591): adom591_FOS-upgrade: { "adom_oid": 591, "data": { "checksum": "1793048616-0646891765", "description": "7.4.12", "enforced version": [ { "flags": 104, "platform": "FGT-Default", "product": 1, "upgrade-path": 1, "version": "7.4.12-b2902" } ], "image-source": null, "schedule-day": null, "schedule-end-time": null, "schedule-start-time": null, "schedule-type": 0 }, "name": "FOS-upgrade", "oid": 6632 }The output is grouped by ADOM. The name and ID of each ADOM are shown in the header line (for example, adom root(3)). An ADOM with no profiles has an empty list.The main fields of each profile are:FieldDescriptionadom_oidObject ID of the ADOM that the profile belongs tonameName of the firmware upgrade profiledescriptionDescription of the profile (for example, the target firmware version)enforced versionTarget firmware for the profile: platform and version/build. null if no version is setschedule-type, schedule-day, schedule-start-time, schedule-end-timeUpgrade schedule of the profile. null if no schedule is configured.image-sourceSource of the firmware image. null if not set.checksumChecksum of the profile dataoidObject ID of the profileClear the firmware upgrade profile database.To clear the firmware upgrade profiles of a specific ADOM, run:diagnose fwmanager profile clear If no ADOM name is specified, the profiles of all ADOMs are cleared:diagnose fwmanager profile clearExample output:clearing fwm profile in adom root(3):... remove adom3_aaa remove adom3_AAA clearing fwm profile in adom FortiCarrier(104):... clearing fwm profile in adom A74(169):... clearing fwm profile in adom ADOMTEST(493):... clearing fwm profile in adom AAA(591):... remove adom591_FOS-upgradeEach remove line shows a profile entry that was removed from the database.Note:The commands are available only in FortiManager 7.2.3, 7.4.0, 7.6.0, 8.0.0 and later. They are not available in earlier builds.Run diagnose fwmanager profile list before and after diagnose fwmanager profile clear to confirm which entries were removed.Running the clear command without an ADOM name affects all ADOMs. Specify the ADOM name to limit the change to one ADOM.

topics.title: Slow dynamic VLAN assignment when using 802.1X and MAC authentication bypass
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a delay in transitioning a FortiSwitch port to the configured Guest VLAN after a RADIUS server rejects an authentication request. Changing the authentication priority in the 802.1X security policy can help reduce the delay.ScopeFortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionSymptomsWhen a device connects to a FortiSwitch port configured for 802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), the port may take approximately one minute to transition from the default VLAN to the configured Guest VLAN after the RADIUS server returns an Access-Reject response.In comparison, when the RADIUS server returns an Access-Accept response, authentication and network access are typically completed much faster.Root CauseThe delay may be related to the authentication priority configured in the 802.1X security policy. When the priority is set to "legacy", the switch may take longer to process the authentication sequence and transition to the Guest VLAN following an authentication failure.ResolutionStep 1: Update the Authentication Priority.Log in to the FortiGate CLI and change the authentication priority from "legacy" to "dot1x-mab" in the applicable 802.1X security policy.config switch-controller security-policy 802-1X edit " " set auth-priority dot1x-mab next endReplace with the name of the applicable 802.1X security policy.This setting prioritizes 802.1X and MAB authentication according to the configured authentication sequence and may reduce the time required to transition to the Guest VLAN after an authentication failure.Step 2: Review the Guest VLAN and Authentication Timeout Settings.Verify that MAB and Guest VLAN assignment are enabled and that the appropriate VLAN is configured in the applicable 802.1X security policy.config switch-controller security-policy 802-1X edit " " set mac-auth-bypass enable set guest-vlan enable set guest-vlan-id " " next endIf the environment requires a VLAN assignment when the RADIUS server times out, review the authentication server timeout VLAN settings supported by the FortiOS version in use. Configure these settings only when the intended behavior is to assign the designated VLAN following a server timeout.Step 3: Review Re-authentication Settings.If the delay persists, review the FortiSwitch 802.1X re-authentication settings. The maximum number of re-authentication attempts can be configured as follows:config switch-controller 802-1X-settings set max-reauth-attempt 0 endStep 4: Verify the configuration.After applying the changes, perform the following checks:Connect a test device that is not authorized for 802.1X authentication to the FortiSwitch port.Check the RADIUS server logs and confirm that the authentication request receives an Access-Reject response.Verify whether MAB authentication is attempted according to the configured authentication sequence and timeout settings.Confirm that the port transitions to the configured Guest VLAN.Verify that the transition time has improved and that authorized devices continue to authenticate and obtain network access as expected.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Explaining 'diagnose traffictest' command limitation on FortiOS
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the limitations of the 'diagnose traffictest' command and how to properly test hardware throughput trafficScopeAll FortiGate models.SolutionIPERF is a tool used for active measurements of the maximum achievable bandwidth on IP networks. FortiGate does have the command 'diagnose traffictest' which is a reduced implementation of IPERF on FortiOS as described in Technical Tip: Use cases for the diagnose traffictest command. The fact that IPERF implementation on FortiGate was reduced can affect the result of bandwidth and throughput tests when they were started from the FortiGate interface instead of having IPERF traffic crossing the FortiGate device. Using a Virtual Machine with Win10 Pro and a NIC of 10Gbps behind the FortiGate 100F for example, that has 2x 10Gbps ports (x1 and x2), is possible to reach ~9Gbps of throughput. Checking the widget of bandwidth on FortiGate for interfaces x1 and x2. Checking IPERF results on VM. Now using the FortiGate 100F x1 interface as the source of the IPERF traffic (IPERF traffic is not crossing the FortiGate), the results are not the same. Checking the widget of bandwidth on FortiGate for interfaces x1 and x2 and IPERF output while the test is still running. The 10Gbps interface x1 cannot reach more than ~900Mbps not because of the hardware throughput, but because of the IPERF reduced implementation on FortiGate. Conclusion: To validate the actual FortiGate throughput and set up the upload and download speed baseline, an external server and client are required to test the throughput with FortiGate in between as the first network diagram presented in this article.Note:The iPerf3 server on the FortiGate cannot be used as a full-featured iPerf3 server.It can be used only for the interface tests between FortiGate ports or as a client towards a server. For tests where an iPerf3 server is required, use a Windows or Linux machine with iPerf3 configured as a server. Related article:Technical Tip: Setting up iperf server and client

topics.title: LDAPS authentication fails due to an incorrect member-attr configuration
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to resolve an issue when users fail to authenticate via LDAPS because the member-attr is incorrectly set to tokenGroups, preventing the FortiGate from matching users to their assigned groups.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionUsers cannot authenticate via LDAPS even though the LDAP server returns a success response. The authentication fails during the group matching phase.The FortiGate is configured to use the tokenGroups attribute to retrieve group memberships. If the Active Directory environment does not populate this attribute or if it is not the correct attribute for the environment, the FortiGate finds zero values and skips group matching, resulting in an authentication failure for the user.Verify the issue via debug:Run the following commands to analyze the authentication process:diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug application fnbamd -1 diagnose debug enableLook for the following indicators in the debug output:attr='tokenGroups' - found 0 values: This indicates the FortiGate is looking for group memberships in the tokenGroups attribute but finding none.find_matched_usr_grps-Skipped group matching: This confirms that because no attributes were found, the user cannot be matched to any group.Correct the member-attr configuration:If tokenGroups is not required by the Active Directory configuration, revert the attribute to the default memberOf.Enter the CLI and navigate to the LDAP server configuration:config user ldap edit set member-attr "memberOf" next endVerify that the user group on the FortiGate references the correct LDAP server and that the LDAP group Distinguished Name (DN) matches the actual group in Active Directory.Additional LDAPS recommendations:When migrating from LDAP to LDAPS, ensure the following:The FortiGate has the appropriate CA certificate installed to validate the LDAP server certificate.The communication is configured over TCP port 636.Server Identity Check is enabled to ensure the certificate matches the configured LDAP server name or IP address.

topics.title: Using FortiAnalyzer to detect activities related to the PHP2Shell RCE Vulnerabilities
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to use a custom event handler in FortiAnalyzer to raise alerts for incident response related to attacks that attempt to leverage the PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619). A report is also provided to gain historical visibility into the logs. Note that this article provides alpha files, which are automatically generated. The article will be continually updated as more information becomes available. Scope This article contains the files necessary to load an event handler and report into the FortiAnalyzer for either a Fabric ADOM or a FortiGate ADOM. The Fabric report and event handler leverage logs from other Fortinet products that can be used to detect the attack in addition to FortiGate logs. For more information about this attack, see the following FortiGuard Outbreak Alert: PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities Solution What is included in Fortinet_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities.zip: PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_event-handler.json: This event handler helps identify PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities detected by FortiGate and other Fortinet products. This event handler is configured for Fabric ADOMs. PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_report.dat: This report displays the findings on PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities from FortiGate and other Fortinet products. It is configured for Fabric ADOMs. fgt_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_event-handler.json: The event handler for FortiGate ADOMs is configured for FortiGate logs only. fgt_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_report.dat: The FortiGate ADOMs report includes only FortiGate charts. Detections included: Product Detection type ID FortiGate IPS signature (attack ID) 62657, 62658 FortiGate OT virtual patch 10009977, 10009978 FortiWeb Signature ID 1090502648 Steps: Download the Fortinet_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities.zip file (contains 4 files). Unzip Fortinet_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities.zip. Import PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_event-handler.json or fgt_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_event-handler.json event handler: Choose an ADOM (if ADOMs are enabled). The ADOM may be of the Fabric or FortiGate type. Go to the Event Handlers module. Select the Import option under More. Select the appropriate event handler depending on the ADOM type. Result: The event handler is enabled and will be triggered if the appropriate logs are received following the import of the event handler. topics.title: Technical Tip: Extended support for v7.0 FIPS-CC Certified/CVE-Patched firmware
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article discusses the v7.0 specialty builds for FIPS-CC certification and the technical support period offered by Fortinet.ScopeFortiGate, FIPS-CC.Solutionv7.0 has passed its End of Engineering Support date (EoES) of 2024-03-30 and will soon be approaching End of Support (EoS) as of 2025-09-30. At the same time, Fortinet only has FIPS-CC Certified/CVE-Patched firmware available for v7.0, as work is still ongoing to have builds for v7.2 and v7.4 certified for FIPS-CC and FIPS 140-3 (see also: NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program - Modules In Process list). Important Updates:2025-10-10: Fortinet has released a candidate build for FortiOS v7.2 FIPS-CC and has made it available for download on the Fortinet Support site. The firmware may be found under the following firmware download section: /FortiGate/v7.00/7.2/FIPS-CC-Certification-Pending/7.2.8-FIPS-CC/FIPS-Candidate.2026-01-19: FortiOS v7.2 FIPS-CC has been certified and has been made available for download on the Fortinet Support site. available for download under section: /FortiGate/v7.00/7.2/FIPS-CC-Certified/7.2.8-FIPS-CC.2025-11-27: Fortinet has also released a candidate build for FortiOS v7.4 FIPS-CC and has made it available for download on the Fortinet Support site. The firmware may be found under the following firmware download section: /FortiGate/v7.00/7.2/FIPS-CC-Certification-Pending/7.4.4-FIPS-CC/FIPS-Candidate.Users currently running the latest FortiOS FIPS-CC v7.0 CVE-Patched build (FIPS-CC-70-21) can upgrade directly to the latest 7.2 FIPS-CC candidate build (FIPS-CC-72-5, at the time of this writing), with no additional upgrade path required.Users who want to upgrade to the latest v7.4 FIPS-CC candidate build should first upgrade from the latest v7.0 FIPS-CC CVE-Patched build to the latest v7.2 FIPS-CC candidate build, then upgrade once again from v7.2 FIPS-CC to v7.4 FIPS-CC.Please note that at the time of this writing, v7.4 has not completed full certification and is still pending final review by NIST. Fully review the ReadMe file in the firmware download folders before installing the firmware in production environments. The original article regarding FortiOS 7.0 FIPS-CC continues below: Fortinet is providing Extended Support specifically for the v7.0 FIPS-CC specialty firmware branch, which includes the original Certified firmware (FIPS-CC-70-6) as well as the subsequent CVE-Patched builds, such as FIPS-CC-70-21 and similar. The following are the key conditions for this Extended Support:Fortinet TAC will continue to offer technical support for clients using the FortiOS v7.0 FIPS-CC specialty firmware, but there will not be extended support for regular v7.0 GA firmware (in the GA case, administrators must upgrade their firmware to a supported release ahead of the EoS date).The Fortinet development team will be specifically providing vulnerability patch support for high- and critical-severity CVEs applicable to v7.0 FIPS for at least the next 12 months, but there will not be any extended support for non-CVE-related bug fixes.Regarding FortiGate Cloud and its enforcement of EoS dates for FortiGate firmware (see also: Requirements):For no-subscription clients, FortiGate Cloud waives the EoS enforcement for FortiGates running in FIPS-CC mode (both for GA firmware as well as the specialty FIPS-CC Certified/CVE-Patched firmware), so users of v7.0 FIPS-CC will retain the ability to integrate with FortiGate Cloud.For subscription clients, EoS enforcement is automatically waived (i.e., subscription users may use any firmware branch regardless of EoS date as long as it is still supported by FortiGate Cloud in general). For further inquiries on the matter, reach out to a regional Fortinet Sales Engineer or contacts within the Fortinet Account team. At the time of this writing, support will currently be extended beyond the v7.0 EoS date by at least 12 months (September 2026).Related article:Technical Tip: How to enable FIPS-CC mode

topics.title: Ring Topology and redundancy protocols
topics.summary: Hi All,I'm looking for guidance and best practices for implementing a resilient Layer 2 access network using a ring topology.Hardware Under ConsiderationFortiGate 121G (Firewall) FortiSwitch FS-1024E (Core/Distribution) FortiSwitch FS-224E (Access) FortiSwitch Rugged FSR-112F-POE (Rugged Access)Design ConsiderationsThe current access-layer design consists of up to five rings, with each ring supporting 15 hops in a dual-ring architecture (up to 30 switches per dual ring).End devices (1 NIC 2 IP ports) will be connecting to two separate access switches for redundancy. The expectation is that RSTP will provide both:Ring redundancy within the access network Redundancy for dual-homed endpoint connectionsThe attached diagram provides a high-level representation of the proposed architecture.Challenges RSTP convergence time RSTP convergence may be too slow for the application. The target recovery/convergence time is less than 1 second following a link or switch failure. MRP/PRP limitations My understanding is that MRP and PRP implementations are typically designed around limited ring structures and may not readily accommodate the proposed multi-ring architecture. Lack of MC-LAG support The selected FSR-112F-POE rugged switch does not support MC-LAG, limiting options for implementing resilient dual-homing at the access layer. Questions1. Alternative redundancy protocolsAre there alternative Layer 2 redundancy protocols or architectures that can achieve sub-second convergence in a network of this size while maintaining ring-based resiliency?2. MRP/PRP scalabilityIf the recommended direction is to use MRP or PRP, would it be feasible to redesign the network into two larger rings, potentially with up to 50 hops per ring?If so:What practical limitations should be considered? How would MRP or PRP operate in a dual-ring design? Are there reference architectures or deployment examples for this type of topology?3. Rugged switch recommendationsGiven the lack of MC-LAG support on the FSR-112F-POE, what alternative ruggedised industrial switch platforms would you recommend that support:Fast Layer 2 recovery (<1 second) Ring protocols (MRP/ERPS or equivalent) MC-LAG or similar dual-homing technologies Integration with a Fortinet-based networkAny design recommendations, deployment experiences, or lessons learned from similar industrial or OT environments would be greatly appreciated.Thanks in advance for your assistance.

topics.title: Resolved: EAPPasswordError with IKEv2, EAP-TTLS and FortiAuthenticator 2FA
topics.summary: I recently encountered and resolved the following issue, and I am sharing the troubleshooting process because the FortiClient error did not immediately indicate the actual cause.EnvironmentFortiClient EMS: 7.4.8 FortiClient for Windows: 7.4.8 FortiAuthenticator: 6.6.9 FortiGate VM: FortiOS 7.4.13 VPN type: IKEv2 IPsec Authentication method: EAP-TTLS User source: LDAP/Active Directory Two-factor authentication: FortiToken managed through FortiAuthenticatorIssueWhen I tried to establish the VPN connection using a domain account, FortiClient returned the following error:EAPPasswordErrorThe authentication process failed, and the VPN connection could not be established.Since I was taking over an existing installation, I was not yet fully familiar with every step of the authentication flow between FortiClient, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, and the LDAP server.Troubleshooting performedI initially verified the following points: The FortiGate was reachable from the client’s public IP address. A direct LDAP authentication test from the FortiGate was successful for both connectivity and credential validation. EAP-TTLS was selected in the VPN profile distributed through FortiClient EMS. EAP-TTLS was enabled in the FortiAuthenticator RADIUS policy, while EAP-MSCHAPv2 was disabled. The default realm configured in the RADIUS policy was associated with the correct LDAP identity source. During an authentication test from FortiAuthenticator, I received an error indicating that the user could not be found in the imported users database. I also found an Access-Reject event containing the message “User Locked”, but I could not confirm whether it was related to the same VPN authentication attempt. Since the direct LDAP test was successful, I initially suspected that the authentication request was not being processed correctly at some point in the chain between IKEv2, EAP-TTLS, RADIUS, FortiAuthenticator, and LDAP.SolutionI eventually found that the problem was related to the way the second authentication factor had to be entered.When EAP-TTLS/PAP is used with two-factor authentication through FortiAuthenticator, FortiClient does not display a separate prompt for the FortiToken code.The LDAP password and the current OTP must be entered consecutively in the same password field:LDAP password + OTPFor example:MyPassword123456After entering the LDAP password followed immediately by the current OTP, the authentication completed successfully and the IKEv2 IPsec VPN connection was established.The behavior and solution are documented in the following Fortinet Technical Tips:Technical Tip: Multi-Factor Authentication support for Windows FortiClient with LDAP (EAP-TTLS)https://community.fortinet.com/fortigate-3/technical-tip-multi-factor-authentication-support-for-windows-forticlient-with-ldap-eap-ttls-212498Technical Tip: How to resolve the “EAP authentication failed due to missing token” error when using EAP-TTLS/PAP + 2FA Authenticationhttps://community.fortinet.com/fortiauthenticator-8/technical-tip-how-to-resolve-the-eap-authentication-failed-due-to-missing-token-error-when-using-eap-ttls-pap-2fa-authentication-216311?tid=216311&fid=8In my case, the issue was not related to LDAP connectivity or realm selection. It was caused by the way the second authentication factor had to be provided when using EAP-TTLS with FortiAuthenticator.The EAPPasswordError message did not immediately indicate the actual cause, and the successful direct LDAP test initially led me to investigate other parts of the authentication flow.Has anyone else encountered the same behavior or received a different FortiClient error in a similar configuration?I hope this information can help anyone troubleshooting the same issue.

topics.title: IPsec VPN SAML SSO authentication with FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes troubleshooting steps for IPsec IKEv2 VPN connections that use SAML single sign-on with FortiGate as the service provider and FortiAuthenticator as the identity provider. It covers troubleshooting listener connectivity, HTTP 403 responses, SAML attributes, and EAP authentication failures. Optional Fortinet Single Sign-On checks are included for deployments that also collect Active Directory logon events.ScopeFortiGate running FortiOS 7.4.11, FortiAuthenticator 6.6.9, and FortiClient 7.4.7 on Windows. The reference lab also used Windows Server 2019 Active Directory and a Windows 10 domain client. Commands and menu paths refer to these versions. Hostnames, usernames, addresses, and object names below are examples.SolutionSymptomsThe lab troubleshooting included the following observations:IKE_SA_INIT and gateway validation completed, but EAP later timed out. The authentication exchange reached a username and candidate group before returning FNBAM_ERROR, with an empty EAP response.After ike-saml-server was configured on the incoming FortiGate interface, the TCP 11443 test succeeded and the FortiClient error changed from Network Error to 403 Forbidden.The second observation establishes progress to an HTTP response. It does not establish successful SAML authentication, completion of EAP, or an operational IPsec tunnel.SolutionIdentify the failing authentication stageFortiClient first reaches the FortiGate IKE SAML listener over HTTPS. The browser is redirected to FortiAuthenticator, which authenticates the user against the configured directory and returns a SAML response to FortiGate. FortiGate then completes the VPN authentication and IKEv2 negotiation. The browser path and the IPsec transport require separate checks.ConnectionPurposeFortiClient to FortiGate TCP 11443Example HTTPS listener for IPsec SAML authenticationClient browser to FortiAuthenticator HTTPSIdentity provider login and SAML exchangeFortiAuthenticator to Active DirectoryDirectory authentication and group lookupFortiClient to FortiGate UDP 500 and 4500IKEv2 and NAT traversal in the reference UDP deploymentVerify DNS reachability and certificates.Run the following PowerShell commands from the affected endpoint before connecting the VPN:Resolve-DnsName vpn.example.com Resolve-DnsName idp.example.com Test-NetConnection vpn.example.com -Port 11443 Test-NetConnection idp.example.com -Port 443Confirm that both names resolve to addresses reachable before VPN establishment.Verify the browser can reach the identity provider over HTTPS.Verify the FortiGate listener certificate covers vpn.example.com, and the FortiAuthenticator HTTPS certificate covers idp.example.com.The endpoint must trust their issuing certificate authorities.Check certificate validity and time synchronization on the endpoint, FortiGate, and FortiAuthenticator.The HTTPS server certificate and the SAML identity provider signing certificate serve different purposes. topics.title: Rx Discards increase on access FortiSwitch uplink ports when fortilink-neighbor-detect is set to FortiLink
topics.summary: DescriptionThe Rx Discards counter increases on the uplink ports of an access FortiSwitch when the FortiGate FortiLink interface uses fortilink-neighbor-detect fortilink. Also, how to stop the increase by changing the setting to LLDP.ScopeFortiGate and FortiSwitch units managed over FortiLink, with fortilink-neighbor-detect set to FortiLink.SolutionSymptoms:The Rx Discards counter increases steadily on the uplink ports of the access FortiSwitch. These are the ports that connect to the distribution or core FortiSwitch.The Rx Discards counter does not increase on the access (downlink) ports.The uplink ports show no CRC, input, or output errors.The Rx Discards counter stops increasing after setting fortilink-neighbor-detect to LLDP on the FortiGate.Cause:When setting fortilink-neighbor-detect to FortiLink, the FortiGate and FortiSwitch units exchange proprietary FortiLink protocol frames over the FortiLink and ISL trunks. The access FortiSwitch receives these frames on its uplink ports, handles them itself instead of forwarding them, and adds them to the Rx Discards counter.When setting fortilink-neighbor-detect to LLDP, the FortiGate and FortiSwitch units use standard LLDP frames for neighbor detection. The FortiSwitch does not add these frames to the Rx Discards counter.Verification:On the FortiGate, check which neighbor detection method the FortiLink interface uses:show full system interface | grep neighborOn the access FortiSwitch, find the uplink trunk and its member ports:diagnose switch trunk summary show switch trunkOn the access FortiSwitch, reset the counters on each uplink port, wait a few minutes, and check the counters again:diagnose switch physical-ports set-counter-zero diagnose switch physical-ports port-stats list Rx Discards: diagnose switch physical-ports list drops Rx Discards: drops set lldp-reception enable set lldp-transmission enable set fortilink-neighbor-detect lldp next endOn the access FortiSwitch, reset the counters on each uplink port and confirm that the Rx Discards counter either stops increasing or no longer increases at the same rate as before the change:diagnose switch physical-ports set-counter-zero diagnose switch physical-ports port-stats list diagnose switch physical-ports list Notes:The increase in the Rx Discards counter does not disrupt production traffic.Changing fortilink-neighbor-detect can briefly interrupt traffic, so plan the change for a maintenance window.Enable LLDP before you change the detection method. If changing the method without enabling LLDP, the managed FortiSwitch units go offline.A FortiLink interface based on a hardware switch does not offer the fortilink-neighbor-detect option.Related Article:Troubleshooting Tip: How to interpret RX drops on FortiSwitch devices

topics.title: Understanding and managing frequent HA audit log 0108035018
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.13, you may observe frequent event logs on a FortiGate High Availability (HA) cluster with log ID 0108035018.A sample log message appears as follows:date=2026-10-23 time=10:33:00 logid="0108035018" type="event" subtype="ha" level="information" vd="root" logdesc="HA secondary received CLI commands" user="FGT_ha_admin" ui="ha_daemon" msg="Received CMD from ip:169.254.0.1 vdom:vsys_ha type:1, msg_type:66"In FortiOS 7.4.13, security audit logging was added to record commands exchanged between HA cluster members across the internal heartbeat channel.Before FortiOS 7.4.13, these internal exchanges occurred silently. topics.title: Metadata variables in CLI scripts use global or default values instead of mapped (per-device/VDOM) values
topics.summary: Description How metadata variables works in a CLI script. Scope FortiManager. Solution Metadata variables referenced inside CLI scripts in FortiManager do not resolve to a device‑specific mapped value when the script is executed on the Device Database. The script applies the value defined for the global context, or the default value if no global value is set — not the value mapped for a specific device or VDOM. Scenario A metadata variable is created with a default value and a per‑device mapped value (e.g. mapped for a root or named VDOM). If used inside a firewall object (e.g. an Address), the variable correctly resolves to the device's mapped value. The same variable used inside a CLI script run on the Device Database resolves to the global value — or the default value when no global value exists — instead of the per‑device/VDOM mapped value. This is an expected behavior. Metadata variables used in CLI scripts executed on the Device Database only support the global context or the default value. VDOM‑context (per‑device/VDOM) mapped values are not resolved within CLI scripts. Below a practical example. This is the metadata variable: FMG_Test # execute fmpolicy print-adom-object 179 3200 test_metadataDump object ttest_metadata] of category dfmg variable] in adom vTEST]:---------------config fmg variableedit "test_metadata"set value "1"config dynamic_mappingedit "Test_Firewall"-"global"set value "5"nextedit "Test_Firewall"-"SDWAN"set value "12"nextedit "Test_Firewall"-"root"set value "9"nextendnextend Script: config vdomedit SDWANconfig router static edit 1 set gateway 1.$(test_metadata).$(test_metadata).4 nextendendconfig vdomedit rootconfig router static edit 1 set gateway 1.$(test_metadata).$(test_metadata).4 nextendend This script is run on the Device DB on Test_Firewall. Note that the "global" value was used. The values assigned to "root" or "SDWAN" were not used. View the log of script Test: running on device Test_Firewall (Test)-------Executing time: Thu Oct 22 15:33:07 2026-----------Starting log (Run on database)config vdomedit SDWANconfig router staticedit 2set gateway 1.5.5.4nextendendconfig vdomedit rootconfig router staticedit 2set gateway 1.5.5.4 nextendendRunning script(Test) on DB success

topics.title: Prevent unnecessary FortiLink frames on FortiSwitch edge ports
topics.summary: DescriptionThe reasons why Managed FortiSwitch ports configured with the default-auto-isl LLDP profile may forward unnecessary FortiLink protocol frames (EtherType 0x88FF) to connected end devices. Devices that do not support or process these frames may discard them, resulting in rapidly increasing packet discard counters and unnecessary network traffic.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionFortiSwitch ports configured with the default-auto-isl LLDP profile by default.This profile supports automatic Inter-Switch Link (ISL) formation, allowing FortiSwitches to discover each other and establish inter-switch trunks.When this profile is applied to ports connected to end devices that do not require automatic ISL formation, FortiLink protocol frames with EtherType 0x88FF may reach those devices.The receiving devices may discard these frames because the EtherType is unsupported, causing unnecessary increases in packet discard counters.SolutionChange the LLDP profile on affected edge ports from default-auto-isl to default.Important: Do not apply this change indiscriminately to ports connected to other FortiSwitches that rely on automatic ISL formation.Configuration via FortiGate CLIIdentify the FortiSwitch and its connected edge ports.Verify that the ports do not require automatic ISL formation.Apply the following configuration:config switch-controller managed-switch edit config ports edit set lldp-profile "default" next end next endExpected resultUnnecessary FortiLink protocol frames are prevented from reaching connected devices on the affected ports, reducing avoidable frame discards and preventing servers from receiving a flood of unnecessary Ethernet frames.

topics.title: FortiAppSec Cookie Security causing HTTP 403 Forbidden errors
topics.summary: DescriptionEnabling the Set HttpOnly Cookie feature in FortiWeb Cloud may cause applications to return HTTP 403 Forbidden errors if the application relies on JavaScript to read CSRF tokens from cookies.ScopeFortiAppSec Cloud.SolutionSymptomsUsers encounter HTTP 403 Forbidden (Authentication Error) responses on various application pages after a successful login. These errors occur specifically when Cookie Security features are enabled in FortiWeb Cloud. No corresponding security violations or blocks appear in the Web Application Firewall (WAF) event logs, even when the policy is set to Alert mode.Root CauseThe issue is caused by the Set HttpOnly Cookie setting. When this feature is enabled, FortiWeb Cloud adds the HttpOnly flag to cookies passed to the browser. This flag prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie.If the application is designed to read a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token from a cookie using JavaScript, the browser cannot access the token. Consequently, the application receives a request with a missing or empty CSRF token and returns an HTTP 403 Access Denied response. Because this is an application-level authentication failure and not a WAF security block, no events are logged in the FortiWeb Cloud WAF logs.ResolutionDisable the Set HttpOnly Cookie option while maintaining other security settings.Log in to the FortiWeb Cloud console.Navigate to the Cookie Security settings for the affected policy.Disable the Set HttpOnly Cookie option.Keep the Set Secure Cookie option enabled if the application supports it.Save the configuration and test the application functionality.

topics.title: How to create a CLI script that runs automatically after every policy package or device settings installation on FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to create a CLI script on FortiManager and configure it to run automatically on the FortiGate after every device install (policy package or device settings installation).ScopeFortiManager 7.x and 8.x.SolutionSome settings are changed or reverted by an install from FortiManager, or cannot be managed from the policy package or device database. A CLI script that runs directly on the FortiGate after each install can restore the required configuration without a manual step.For this, create a script with the target "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)", then enable "Automatic execute after each device install" in the script schedule.Step 1: Create the scriptGo to "Device Manager" -> Script.Select "Create New".Enter a name for the script (for example, "post-install-script").Set "Type" to "CLI Script".Set "Run script on" to "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)".In "Script Detail", enter the CLI commands to run on the FortiGate. For example, for a FortiGate with VDOMs enabled:config vdom edit root config set end next endFor a FortiGate without VDOMs, enter the commands without the "config vdom" and "edit root" lines:config set endSelect "OK".Step 2: Run the script automatically after every installEnable the scheduled and automatic script options in the FortiManager CLI:config system admin setting set show_automatic_script enable set show_schedule_script enable endGo to "Device Manager" -> "Scripts".Right-click the CLI script and select "Schedule Script".Select the FortiGate devices that the script will run on.Select "Enable Automatic execute after each device install".Select "OK".Once enabled, the script runs on the selected FortiGate devices after each install, including every policy package installation and device settings installation. No manual step is needed.VerificationInstall a policy package or the device settings to one of the selected FortiGate devices.When the installation finishes, go to "Device Manager" -> "Scripts" and open the script execution history ("Script Log") to check that the script ran on the device.On the FortiGate CLI, check that the configuration was applied. For example:show full | grep Note:"Automatic execute after each device install" is only available when "Run script on" is set to "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)". It cannot be used with scripts that target "Policy Package" or "ADOM Database".When "Automatic execute after each device install" is enabled, a time-based schedule (one time, daily, weekly, monthly) cannot be configured for the same script.A script that runs directly on the FortiGate triggers an automatic retrieve back to FortiManager. The policy package status may temporarily show "Unknown".The script runs after the install, so the change is applied on the FortiGate but does not become part of the policy package or the device database in FortiManager. The next install can overwrite it, which is why the script runs after every install.Related documents:Troubleshooting Tip: Useful workaround when FortiManager does not install configuration as expectedTechnical Tip: CLI Script behavior to run in FortiManager

topics.title: Windows updates fails with enabled Forticlient
topics.summary: Since last week we experiencing a lot of problems with Windows updates (mostly Windows 11, but there was one Windows 10 among them as well), specifically KB5040442. On about 10% of our Windows clients the update would start and go until 96% and stay there for 10-60 minutes, and then after a restart Windows would tell us that something did go wrong and it would reverse the update. This would require multiple restarts and anything in the order of 2-10h. The usual information sources did not reveal anything unusual with this update round, so it had to be some uncommon conditions here. When Windows was back online, it would sometimes (!) show an error code 0x800f0922, oftenly nothing, and on next restart it would try to install it again (and our employees losing again 4-10h with a working computer). First remedy, as described in the error code was to increase the size of the recovery partition to at least 250MB, but that helped only on one computer. No other things related to the code did apply to us or help. DISM and SFC sometimes would find something, but did not help in fixing the issues with the update. Over time some of the computers randomly succeeded in installing the update. Last straw I had was to disable and uninstall Forticlient. And with that so far all of the clients went through the update without a hitch. Now I am anxious that it will return with the next update when I reinstall Forticlient. In retrospective, two computers had some troubles with some previous updates, but we re-installed Windows on them. Both were also affected this time. What should be do and how can we prevent that from happening again? Is there anything to further debug and diagnose this issue? For your reference we use Forticlient 7.2.4.0972 with EMS, and a Fortigate 200F as main firewalls. We have the web filter, AV and real-time protection enabled, as well as Anti-malware, Anti-Exploit and Cloud-base malware protection. Thank you in advance for your help. Regards,Markus

Fortinet has released a special build to address the issue. Contact Fortinet Technical Support to validate whether the issue applies to the affected device and obtain the appropriate special build. topics.title: FortiAP 231K Repeated cwWtpd / lldpd Restarts and CAPWAP Failure
topics.summary: Hello Fortinet Community,We are facing a persistent issue with a FortiAP 231K that fails to come online on our FortiGate 60E. Interestingly, the same behavior has also been observed on the replacement FortiAP received through RMA.We would appreciate guidance from the community or Fortinet engineers who may have encountered similar symptoms.EnvironmentFortiGate: FortiGate 60E FortiOS: 7.4.12 Access Point: FortiAP 231K AP management: FortiGate wireless controller Original testing topology: FortiGate -> PoE switch -> FortiAP 231K Replacement AP testing setup: PoE injector -> FortiAP 231K, with a laptop connected for testing and a serial console connection through PuTTYWe have checked the official FortiAP and FortiOS Compatibility Matrix and are investigating the issue using the supported firmware combination listed for the FortiAP 231K and FortiOS 7.4.12.Issue ObservedThe FortiAP boots successfully but does not come online or establish a stable CAPWAP connection with the FortiGate.The PuTTY console repeatedly displays the following messages:process '/usr/sbin/lldpd' (pid 16561) exited. Scheduling for restart.process '/sbin/cwWtpd' (pid 16563) exited. Scheduling for restart.ERROR!!! Send debug config info to capwap failedThese messages continue appearing repeatedly while the AP remains powered on.Troubleshooting PerformedWe have performed the following checks:Performed multiple factory resets. Verified that the AP boots successfully and that serial console access is available. Confirmed that the FortiGate wireless controller is enabled. Tested the original AP through different PoE switch ports. Left the AP running for 10–15 minutes to check whether it would come online. Tried Deauthorize/Authorize and Reject/Authorize actions from the FortiGate. Collected PuTTY console logs and video recordings showing the repeated process restarts. Verified that another FortiAP operates normally under the same FortiGate wireless controller. Tested the replacement AP separately using a PoE injector, laptop, and serial console connection rather than connecting it directly to the FortiGate for this test.Despite these tests, the replacement AP exhibits the same repeated process restarts.Important ObservationThe original FortiAP 231K exhibited these symptoms and was approved for RMA due to the repeated daemon restart issue. However, the replacement FortiAP 231K has now exhibited the same behavior during separate testing using a PoE injector, laptop, and console connection.Since the same symptoms have appeared on both units, we would like to determine whether this could be related to firmware/software, AP initialization, or another underlying issue rather than two independent hardware failures.Questions for the Community Has anyone encountered repeated cwWtpd and lldpd restarts on a FortiAP 231K? Could ERROR!!! Send debug config info to capwap failed indicate a known firmware or CAPWAP issue? Are there specific CLI commands or debug outputs we should collect to identify why these processes keep restarting? Could the same symptoms occur when the AP is powered through a PoE injector and tested separately from the FortiGate's direct physical connection? Are there known certificate-related or controller compatibility issues that could cause this behavior on a FortiGate 60E? Has anyone successfully resolved this issue while remaining on the FortiOS 7.4.x branch? We would appreciate any troubleshooting suggestions, known bug references, or recommended fixes. Upgrading the production FortiGate to a different major firmware branch is not currently feasible, so guidance applicable to our existing environment would be especially helpful.Thank you for your time and assistance.

topics.title: FortiClient VPN 7.4.3 (macOS) drops IPsec IKEv2 tunnel immediately on screen lock - "Check VPN Connect without Reauth"
topics.summary: Environment:- FortiClient VPN (free, VPN-only) 7.4.3.4323- macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 (iMac)- IPsec IKEv2 tunnel with SAML SSO/MFA, NAT-T (UDP 4500)- Not connected to EMS (log shows "Ignore Secure compliance Check as FCT is not connected to EMS")Problem:The VPN tunnel is disconnected by FortiClient itself less than one second after the macOS screen is locked. This happens even when the system is prevented from sleeping (display sleep and screensaver disabled, sleep prevented with a keep-awake utility) and while traffic is actively flowing through the tunnel.Steps to reproduce:1. Connect the IPsec IKEv2 tunnel with SAML SSO.2. Keep traffic flowing through the tunnel (e.g. a TCP check every 60 seconds to an internal host).3. Disable screensaver and display sleep, prevent system sleep.4. Lock the screen (Ctrl+Cmd+Q).5. The tunnel is disconnected within ~0.7 seconds.If the screen is not locked, the tunnel stays up indefinitely, so this is not an idle timeout, a network issue, or a gateway-side disconnect.Relevant unified log entries (log show, IPs redacted):11:02:38.179 iked: com.fortinet.forticlient:IPSec] ikev2_ike_sa_alive: sending alive check11:02:38.194 iked: :com.fortinet.forticlient:IPSec] recv INFORMATIONAL res 409 peer :4500 ... policy 'vpn'11:02:38.194 iked: dcom.fortinet.forticlient:IPSec] ikev2_msg_decrypt: integrity check succeeded11:02:39.731 loginwindow: _handleAppleEvent | Received a kAELockScreenEvent11:02:40.394 FortiTray: rcom.fortinet.forticlient.macos:util] Check VPN Connect without Reauth11:02:40.432 FortiTray: Tcom.fortinet.forticlient.macos:util] VPN disconnected11:02:40.508 FortiTray: icom.fortinet.forticlient.macos:util] Config firewall policy succeededThe IKE SA keepalive succeeds one second before the lock, so the tunnel is healthy. The disconnect is initiated locally by FortiTray right after the lock event, following the "Check VPN Connect without Reauth" step.Questions:1. Is disconnecting on screen lock intended behavior for IPsec tunnels with SAML SSO on macOS?2. Is there a setting (client-side, FortiGate-side, or XML config) to keep the tunnel up while the session is locked, and is it available in the free VPN-only client without EMS?3. Does the Windows client behave the same way with the same tunnel configuration?This makes the client hard to use for remote work: users must either leave the workstation unlocked (a security issue) or re-authenticate with MFA every time they step away.Thanks.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Retrieve configuration file using GUI or CLI from a FortiManager
topics.summary: Description This article describes how the configuration file of a FortiGate can be retrieved by a FortiManager through the GUI or the CLI. Retrieving the configuration file using CLI can be used to gather more debug information if the retrieval process fails in the GUI. Scope FortiManager. Solution Via GUI: From: Device Manager -> Device & Group, as shown below: Select the managed FortiGate for which it is necessary to retrieve the configuration. Scroll down until the section: Configuration and Installation is visible; Click the button to the right of the Total Revision number called: Revision history. In the section that appears on the right, there is the Retrieve config button. Via CLI: Use the following debug to retrieve the OID of the device in question: diagnose dvm device list Once the OID value is known, the following command can be executed to retrieve the configuration file of the device in question: diagnose test deploymanager reloadconf <----- OID value from the previous step. Sample Configuration: diagnose dvm device list --- There are currently 2 devices/vdoms managed --- TYPE OID SN HA IP NAME ADOM IPS FIRMWARE fmg/faz enabled 158 FGVM0X00000XXXX - 10.5.60.3 FGVM010000****** root 6.00741 (regular) 5.0 MR4 (7605) |- STATUS: db: not modified; conf: out of sync; cond: unknown; dm: autoupdated; conn: down |- vdom:[3]root flags:1 adom:root pkg:[imported]FGVM010000****** Where the OID will be 158 for the respective FortiGate: diagnose test deploymanager reloadconf 158 Note: This operation is possible if the FGFM tunnel between the FortiGate and the FortiManager is up; otherwise, it will be necessary to perform troubleshooting as explained in Troubleshooting Tip: How to troubleshoot connectivity issues The following is an explanation of when it is useful to perform the Retrieve: FortiManager device settings and sync status Related articles: Technical Tip: How to fix synchronization issue in FortiManager Technical Tip: How to do bulk retrieve config in FortiManager using a script

topics.title: FortiNAC-F does not assign a VLAN via MAB to FortiAPs managed by a FortiGate
topics.summary: DescriptionReasons why FortiNAC-F answers MAB requests for FortiGate-managed FortiAPs with an Access-Accept that carries no VLAN, and how to fix it. The fix is one global setting: Enable Network Access Policy for Wireless Access Points, under System -> Settings -> Network Device.ScopeFortiNAC-F 7.6.x (validated on 7.6.7).FortiGate acting as wireless controller for FortiAPs, modeled in FortiNAC Network -> Inventory.FortiAPs connected to a third-party access switch (example: Aruba CX 6200) that uses FortiNAC as RADIUS server for MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB).SolutionSymptoms:The FortiAP's switch port stays in the static access VLAN instead of moving to the VLAN set in the Network Access Policy.The FortiAP appears under the FortiGate in Network -> Inventory as a Wireless Access Point.Searching the AP MAC in Users & Hosts -> Hosts returns nothing.Device Profiling Rules (for example Vendor OUI, type Wireless Access Point) never process the AP.Network Access Policies whose User/Host Profile matches the AP MAC never match.Deleting the AP from Inventory makes the policy work temporarily; the AP returns under the FortiGate at the next poll or reconnect.The RADIUS log shows an Access-Accept with no VLAN attributes (example values):[Access-Request] AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF USER [aabbccddeeff] DEVICE [10.0.0.10] ATTRIBUTES [ User-Name = aabbccddeeff, Service-Type = Call-Check, Calling-Station-Id = AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF, NAS-Identifier = ACCESS-SW-01, NAS-Port-Type = Ethernet, NAS-Port-Id = 1/1/2 ] [Access-Accept] AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF USER [aabbccddeeff] DEVICE [10.0.0.10] ATTRIBUTES [ REST-HTTP-Status-Code = 200, Cleartext-Password = "aabbccddeeff", Class = 0x..., Hint = "...", Tmp-String-1 = "request" ]The Access-Accept carries no Tunnel-Type, Tunnel-Medium-Type or Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, so the switch keeps the port in its default VLAN.Cause:This is expected behavior. FortiNAC models FortiGate-managed FortiAPs as network devices (Inventory elements), not as hosts. When a Wireless Access Point connects to a managed switch port, FortiNAC changes the port type to WAP Uplink.By default, FortiNAC does not evaluate Network Access Policies for Wireless Access Points and does not enforce any policy on a WAP Uplink port. With no host record and no applicable policy, the MAB Access-Accept carries no VLAN.SolutionEnable Network Access Policy evaluation for Wireless Access Points. No other change is required when the Network Access Policy and port configuration are already in place.In the FortiNAC GUI, go to System -> Settings -> Network Device.Select Enable Network Access Policy for Wireless Access Points.Select Save Settings.Confirm the switch port where the FortiAP connects is a member of the Role-Based Access port group. This is required for the setting to take effect.Optional: Set Wireless Access Point Enforcement Group to a port group. FortiNAC adds a port to it when a Wireless Access Point connects; it does not remove the port automatically.Reconnect the FortiAP or bounce its switch port so a new MAB request is sent.Verification:The RADIUS Access-Accept for the AP MAC now includes Tunnel-Type = VLAN, Tunnel-Medium-Type = IEEE-802 and Tunnel-Private-Group-ID = the policy VLAN.Network -> Inventory -> switch -> Ports: The AP port shows the expected VLAN, and Port Changes records the change.Verify the VLAN assigned to the switch port interface.Notes:Deleting FortiAPs from Inventory is not a workaround; FortiNAC re-adds them under the FortiGate.The AP port must not be in the Authorized Access Points group, which prevents VLAN switching on the port.If the port is also in Reset Forced Default, set its Default VLAN equal to the policy VLAN to avoid the VLAN cycling between the two.Confirm RADIUS and VLAN switching are enabled in the switch Model Configuration, with a RADIUS attribute group that includes RFC VLAN attributes.Tunnel-mode SSIDs are preferred. With bridge-mode SSIDs, wireless client MACs also appear on the AP port, which can affect port classification and MAB on the switch.Alternative: Network Device Roles (role assigned to the FortiAP + mapping by port group and VLAN), with the port in Role-Based Access.Related articles:Administration Guide (FortiNAC-F 7.6): Network device settingsAdministration Guide (FortiNAC-F 7.6): Network device rolesWAP behavior when connected to WAP Uplink ports

topics.title: Technical Tip: How to configure Network ID for distinguishing IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels using FortiClient XML file
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article explains how to edit the FortiClient XML file to distinguish multiple IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels using Network ID instead of Peer ID.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient.SolutionWhen multiple dial-up IPsec IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels are configured on FortiGate, a unique Network ID must be defined on each Phase 1 configuration. This allows FortiGate to correctly match incoming IKEv2 initiations with the appropriate tunnel.If the Network ID is not defined, FortiGate cannot reliably determine which Phase 1 configuration to use when multiple IKEv2 dial‑up tunnels reside on the same interface. This behavior differs from IKEv1, where Peer IDs were used to distinguish between tunnels. Use the following CLI syntax to define the Network ID for each Phase 1 configuration: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit " " set ike-version 2 set network-overlay enable set network-id next end The Network ID must be defined on both the FortiGate Phase1 and the FortiClient configuration to ensure correct tunnel matching.Note: The Network ID setting cannot be configured on unmanaged or standalone Forticlient. For managed Forticlient, configuration of Network ID is supported through Forticlient EMS starting with versions 7.2.6 and later or 7.4.1 and later.The FortiClient XML configuration file can be manually edited or provisioned via EMS with the Network ID attribute. Locate the section of the XML, and insert the tag as shown below.Note: Occasionally, this value is not included in the configuration. In that case, manually add the section as shown below. 2 2 In this example, '2' represents the Network ID and must match the corresponding Phase 1 configuration on the FortiGate.Ensure that the tag is placed within the correct tunnel definition block in the XML file.Result:After importing the modified XML configuration into FortiClient, the IKEv2 initiator message will include the Network ID.This allows FortiGate to correctly match the proper Phase 1 configuration even when multiple IKEv2 dial‑up tunnels share the same interface.The configured Network ID must be unique for each IKEv2 tunnel, allowing the FortiGate to distinguish and correctly select the intended Phase 1 configuration.
