topics.title: Preserving client IP addresses across AP group VLANs with Layer 3 intra controller roaming
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to enable a new Layer 3 intra-controller roaming feature on a bridge-mode SSID, so wireless clients can move between FortiAP groups that are mapped to different VLANs, while retaining their original IP address.ScopeFortiGate 60F with FortiOS 7.4.11 and two FortiAP-441K access points with FortiAP firmware 7.6.3, managed by the same FortiGate.The source lab used feature-specific STS builds. The version labels above identify the tested release families and do not establish support in every build. Confirm that the target build exposes 'l3-intra-roaming' before applying this configuration.Solution1. Prepare the environmentUse two authorized FortiAPs managed by the same FortiGate and broadcasting the same bridge-mode SSID. Configure the SSID authentication before applying the following changes. The selected test used WPA2 Personal.Create two managed AP groups and assign one access point to each:FortiAPAP groupClient VLANManagement IPFAP1-loungeNorth10010.10.201.2FAP2-officeSouth20010.10.202.2Provide the required VLANs, DHCP scopes, gateways, and routing. Ensure the FortiAPs can communicate directly, without NAT in the path, when using direct roaming mode.Advertise the SSID on both access points. The tested 5 GHz channels were 140 and 132. Adjust transmit power to provide overlapping coverage and allow the client to select another access point when moving. Check the RF environment before starting the test.2. Map the AP groups to VLANs and enable intra-controller roamingOn the FortiGate, edit the existing SSID object. Replace with its configured name. The groups North and South must already exist and contain the corresponding access points.config wireless-controller vap edit " " set local-bridging enable set vlan-pooling wtp-group config vlan-pool edit 100 set wtp-group "North" next edit 200 set wtp-group "South" next end set l3-roaming enable set l3-intra-roaming enable set l3-roaming-mode direct next endThe key setting is 'set l3-intra-roaming enable' in the SSID configuration. The VLAN pool associates each participating AP group with its local client VLAN. Configure both groups; enabling the roaming setting alone does not replace this mapping.These changes modify an existing SSID, not a complete SSID creation script. Preserve the existing authentication and radio assignments. Review existing VLAN pool entries before applying the example.3. Validate IP preservationConnect a client to the SSID and record its IP address, associated FortiAP, and VLAN. Start a continuous connectivity test to a reachable destination. Move the client between the coverage areas, then return to the original access point.In the FortiGate wireless client monitor, compare the IP, FortiAP, FortiAP IP, and VLAN fields. The access point and local VLAN context should change while the client IP remains unchanged during the roaming test.Figure 1: iPhone test across FAP1-lounge (VLAN 100) and FAP2-office (VLAN 200). Both records show the client IP 10.10.200.3. Customer SSID labels are redacted.Figure 2: The iPhone is shown back on FAP2-office in VLAN 200 with the same IP, 10.10.200.3.Figure 3: Android test showing the same client IP, 10.10.100.2, across the two FortiAPs and VLAN contexts.Figure 4: Windows test showing client IP 10.10.200.4 across the same VLAN 100 and VLAN 200 roaming path. Customer SSID and personal device labels are redacted.The tested monitor sometimes retained duplicate client records after roaming. The paired rows show the observed IP and VLAN contexts; they do not prove simultaneous associations. Correlate the monitor with reassociation events and the client-side connectivity test.ResultThe selected local-lab test successfully validated roaming between North/VLAN 100 and South/VLAN 200 with iPhone, Android, and Windows clients retaining their original IP addresses. The report also records successful return to the original access point.IP preservation applies to the tested roaming sequence. It does not imply that a client keeps its address indefinitely after disconnecting or rehoming. The results do not establish zero packet loss or a universal roaming-time guarantee.

topics.title: Capturing Zebra ZS300 BLE data with FortiAP for temperature monitoring
topics.summary: DescriptionConfigure BLE scanning on a FortiAP to collect advertisements from Zebra ZS300 temperature sensors for processing and visualization by an external application.ScopeThe main proof of concept used a FortiGate 60F running FortiOS 7.4.12 and a FortiAP-233G running firmware 7.4.5. A separate local validation used a FortiAP-234F.The workflow illustrates BLE scanning on both models. Configuration availability depends on the FortiAP model and firmware.Solution1. Configure BLE scanningOn the FortiGate, create a BLE profile using the scan parameters validated during the proof of concept:config wireless-controller ble-profile edit "ZEBRA-ZS300-BLE" set ble-scanning enable set scan-type active set scan-threshold "-90" set scan-period 4000 set scan-time 1000 set scan-interval 50 set scan-window 50 next endAssign the BLE profile to the FortiAP profile. Replace with the existing profile name.config wireless-controller wtp-profile edit " " set ble-profile "ZEBRA-ZS300-BLE" next endIf the FortiAP profile is shared, this change affects the other access points using it.2. Verify the BLE configurationFrom the FortiAP CLI, run:cw_diag -c ble-configThe following excerpt shows the scan configuration observed during the main proof of concept:WTP Bluetooth Low Energy Configuration: ble scan report interval : 30 ble scanning : enabled (mode=active,thresh=-90,period=4000,time=1000,intv=50,wind=50)BLE scanning must be enabled. The iBeacon and Eddystone advertising settings also displayed by this command describe advertisements transmitted by the FortiAP and are not required to interpret the Zebra sensor data.3. Verify sensor receptionPlace the active sensor within BLE coverage and run:cw_diag -c ble-scanThe following output is transcribed from the local validation screenshot:BLE_DEV (001/001), mac ce:c3:25:fc:4e:a0 gen : 1 rssi : -88 addr type : random name : GEOMOV14587_LE manufacture : first seen : Mar 17 14:55:48 last seen : Mar 17 14:55:48 channel : 38 raw data : 22 0201020f0947454f 4d4f563134353837 5f4c45020a00Use the known sensor MAC address and its serial-number mapping in the sensor inventory to identify the intended device. Check the reception timestamps, RSSI, and raw data field.For devices using random BLE addresses, verify the identity mapping instead of assuming that the displayed address remains permanent.Figure 1: BLE configuration and scan output from the FortiAP-234F used for local validation. The main laboratory used a FortiAP-233G. The screenshot illustrates the scan workflow on another model; it does not independently demonstrate Zebra temperature decoding.4. Display temperature dataDuring the proof of concept, an external collector accessed the FortiAP over SSH through an IPsec VPN and retrieved BLE scan output every five seconds. The external application identified the Zebra sensor, processed the captured payload, and displayed temperature information in a dashboard.The FortiAP provided BLE scan data. The external application decoded the payload, stored historical data, and visualized it on a dashboard.Figure 2: Dashboard supplied as evidence of the proof of concept. The displayed period includes 12,044 events, an average RSSI of -78 dBm, an average battery level of 68.5%, and an average temperature of -19.01 °C. The dashboard also displays a mean kinetic temperature of -19.18 °C. These values are aggregated metrics, not individual instantaneous measurements.Note: Restrict SSH access to the authorized collector and protect its credentials. The five-second collection interval is independent of the BLE report interval shown by ble-config and does not guarantee a new temperature measurement on each query. Validate collection performance and the automation method before production deployment.

topics.title: RMA Information: Hardware failure and replacement with a spare unit on-site (support procedure)
topics.summary: Description This KB article describes, how to manage an RMA request (a hardware replacement request within the technical support contract) with the Fortinet Customer Service and Support (Fortinet CSS), when another (possibly temporary) spare unit is already available on-site. In case of a hardware failure on a Fortinet product and a need for replacement, when a spare unit is already available on-site (for example: a "cold spare" unit, or a temporarily loaned unit from a Fortinet reseller or distributor), for a smooth RMA exchange of the defective unit by the Fortinet CSS, Fortinet recommends to proceed as follows: 1. With the Fortinet CSS, create an RMA ticket first, using the serial number of the defective unit.2. In the RMA ticket, describe the problem with the defective unit, and make sure to mention to which spare/replacement unit (specify the serial number) the support contract will be transferred to.3. Once the RMA ticket has been created, request the Fortinet Customer Service (Fortinet CS) to transfer the support contract from the defective unit to the spare unit, possibly by creating another ticket (this time, a CS ticket), or making a phone call. Important step is to create an RMA ticket with Fortinet before transfering the support contract and all FortiGuard service subscriptions to the spare/replacement unit. Proceeding this way will prevent the defective unit to be considered as not covered by a valid support contract later on, resulting in an RMA refusal by Fortinet internal customer support systems. For more information on how to contact Fortinet CSS, please see our Contact Us page and refer to the Ticket Creation Guide, available for download on the Fortinet support portal (on the main Fortinet website, select Service & Support > Support Login > login with your credentials).

topics.title: Taking over a messy production FortiManager (100+ FortiGates, many ADOMs): safest way to reconcile drift and standardise policy?
topics.summary: I've been brought in to help an organisation with a large branch network get proper value from their FortiManager. It was set up by someone else and never became the single source of truth. They want to push policies, templates, firmware and switch and AP settings from FortiManager, with no policy mismatches and no per-firewall changes. It's a live environment, so any approach has to avoid outages.EnvironmentFortiManager VM 7.6.x in HA, with several ADOMs100+ FortiGates (mixed 60F, 40F and 100F class units) all on the same FortiOS 7.4.x buildA large number of FortiSwitches and FortiAPs through FortiLinkHub-and-spoke SD-WAN, which works fine and is out of scopeWhat I found (read-only access)Far more policy packages than makes sense for the number of devices, and many devices have a package to themselves. This looks like cloned packages instead of meta variables and dynamic mappings.A number of devices show Modified config status, concentrated in one ADOM, and I haven't seen any Synchronized devices. Most show Auto-update.A handful of devices show Never Installed.One ADOM is still set to an older version than the FortiOS its devices run.Several ADOMs hold the same branch hardware, so each change has to be repeated in each one.Very few provisioning templates (SD-WAN only), no system templates for NTP, DNS, admin or logging, and a separate firmware template per ADOM.The last FortiManager backup is a couple of months old.My planFresh backup and a change freeze on direct firewall changes.Read-only baseline: revision history and package comparison on the Modified devices.Upgrade the older ADOM after a lab rehearsal.Build a few role-based packages with meta variables, then merge the per-device copies.Retrieve and import the config for the Never Installed devices before assigning anything.Run Install Preview with line-by-line review, and migrate in waves (pilot sites first, hubs last).Consolidate the duplicate branch ADOMs into one at the end.I plan to rehearse everything first on a lab ADOM, using spare FortiGates that were retired from sites.QuestionsFor a Modified device, how do you safely work out what the pending changes are, and then decide whether to keep or discard them before an install?How do you merge per-device packages into shared ones safely? Do you use package diff and clone, or rebuild with meta variables and dynamic mappings?For devices that were added but never had policy installed, what's the safest way to bring them under management without overwriting a working config? Import, then Install Preview?Is moving devices between ADOMs to consolidate them worth the risk, or do you keep separate ADOMs and standardise through the Global ADOM instead?What does the Auto-update config status mean in practice, and should I worry when it appears on almost every device?Any pitfalls with running devices on a newer FortiOS than their ADOM version, and with upgrading that ADOM?How do you structure a lab ADOM so it can't affect production (VPN settings, shared Global policy, licence use)?Any other traps you've hit taking over an inherited FortiManager?Thanks in advance. Happy to share more detail (sanitised) if it helps.What I changedNo industry, no counts, no exact version numbers beyond the major branch, and no licence figures.I removed the "financial services" detail, since that narrows the field a lot.Nothing in it names a client, host, serial, IP or ADOM.

For example:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "custom-deep-inspection" config https set udp-not-quick allow end config dot set udp-not-quick allow end next endWhen installing on FortiGate models with 2GB of memory, this change causes the installation to fail.These models do not support this option in FortiOS version 7.6.This behavior is due to a known issue, with ID 1352524 Contournement : Set 'udp-not-quic' to 'block' in the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Set udp-not-quic to block in the https and dot sections of the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Go to Policy & Objects -> Advanced.Select the CLI Configurations tab.In the left pane, under firewall, select ssl-ssh-profile.Select the affected profile (for example, custom-deep-inspection), then select Edit.In the Edit firewall ssl-ssh-profile window, scroll to the https section and set udp-not-quic to block.Scroll to the dot section and set udp-not-quic to block.Select OK.Repeat steps 4 to 7 for each SSL/SSH profile that is used by the 2GB FortiGate devices.Install the policy package again.Note: Some models may not accept this setting. For example, a comment on this article reports 'Operation not supported. detail: object not support' on a FortiGate 50G. Contact Fortinet Support if the error persists.Fix: A fix is expected in FortiManager firmware versions 7.6.9 and 8.0.3.Related document:Known issues

incidents.title: 1GbE SFP ports may fail to forward traffic on FortiGate 1800F/1801F after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.summary: Description This articles describes an issue where the 1GbE SFP ports may fail to forward traffic on FortiGate 1800F/1801F after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8 Scope FortiGate 1800F, FortiGate 1801F, FortiOS 7.6.8 Solution Following an internal driver update introduced in FortiOS 7.6.8, the affected platforms - FortiGate 1800F and 1801F is unable to process traffic over its GE SFP slots. As a summary:GE SFP ports 17-24 are unable to process traffic.Traffic through SFP ports 25-40 is unaffected.Traffic through GE RJ45 ports is unaffected.

incidents.title: FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number for synchronized tags, preventing ZTNA access for tagged devices.ScopeFortiPAM, FortiClient EMS.SolutionDevices with assigned tags in FortiClient EMS cannot access FortiPAM via ZTNA. The tags synchronized from FortiClient EMS to FortiPAM are associated with an incorrect serial number that does not match the actual FortiClient EMS console serial number.
incidents.symptom: FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number for synchronized tags, preventing ZTNA access for tagged devices
incidents.solution: Devices with assigned tags in FortiClient EMS cannot access FortiPAM via ZTNA. The tags synchronized from FortiClient EMS to FortiPAM are associated with an incorrect serial number that does not match the actual FortiClient EMS console serial number. Root CauseFortiPAM retrieves the default tenant serial number instead of the specific tenant serial number in multi-tenant FortiClient EMS environments. This is identified as BUG 1343587. Permanent FixUpdate FortiClient EMS to version 7.4.9 or later Contournement : Perform the following steps to clear the invalid tags and refresh the synchronization: Clear the invalid tags associated with the incorrect serial number by running the following command on FortiPAM: diagnose endpoint tags remove-by-sn Restart the fabric connector daemon to refresh the data: diag test app fcnacd 99 Verify that the tags are synchronized with the correct serial number using the following commands: diagnose test application fcnacd 2 diagnose test application fcnacd 7

incidents.title: Slow dynamic VLAN assignment when using 802.1X and MAC authentication bypass
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a delay in transitioning a FortiSwitch port to the configured Guest VLAN after a RADIUS server rejects an authentication request. Changing the authentication priority in the 802.1X security policy can help reduce the delay.ScopeFortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionSymptomsWhen a device connects to a FortiSwitch port configured for 802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), the port may take approximately one minute to transition from the default VLAN to the configured Guest VLAN after the RADIUS server returns an…
incidents.symptom: This article describes a delay in transitioning a FortiSwitch port to the configured Guest VLAN after a RADIUS server rejects an authentication request. Changing the authentication priority in the 802.1X security policy can help reduce the delay
incidents.solution: SymptomsWhen a device connects to a FortiSwitch port configured for 802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), the port may take approximately one minute to transition from the default VLAN to the configured Guest VLAN after the RADIUS server returns an Access-Reject response.In comparison, when the RADIUS server returns an Access-Accept response, authentication and network access are typically completed much faster.Root CauseThe delay may be related to the authentication priority configured in the 802.1X security policy. When the priority is set to "legacy", the switch may take longer to process the authentication sequence and transition to the Guest VLAN following an authentication failure.ResolutionStep 1: Update the Authentication Priority.Log in to the FortiGate CLI and change the authentication priority from "legacy" to "dot1x-mab" in the applicable 802.1X security policy.config switch-controller security-policy 802-1X edit " " set auth-priority dot1x-mab next endReplace with the name of the applicable 802.1X security policy.This setting prioritizes 802.1X and MAB authentication according to the configured authentication sequence and may reduce the time required to transitio

aiReview.symptom: Lorsqu'un appareil se connecte à un port FortiSwitch configuré pour le 802.1X et le MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), le port peut mettre environ une minute pour passer du VLAN par défaut au VLAN invité après une réponse Access-Reject du serveur RADIUS.
aiReview.solution: Se connecter à la CLI du FortiGate et modifier la priorité d'authentification de « legacy » à « dot1x-mab » dans la politique de sécurité 802.1X concernée.

incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue affecting FortiGate G-Series devices where downgrading or upgrading from v8.0.1 to v8.0.x via the GUI fails, displaying the error status 'Upgrade Failed'
incidents.solution: Example error: During the firmware upgrade attempt, the device status may display the following:Steps to replicate the issue: Log in to a FortiGate G-Series device running FortiOS v8.0.1 build 0245 (Feature).Attempt to upgrade the firmware to FortiOS v8.0.2 using the online upgrade method via FortiGate Cloud or the GUI.Observe that the firmware upgrade fails. incidents.title: FortiManager policy package import error "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device"
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to troubleshoot and fix an import error issue when it shows "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device".ScopeFortiManager, FortiGate.SolutionWhen FortiManager import policy package from FortiGate shows fails as following:The Download Import Report shows as following:"system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-IP-BlockList1, oid=2634, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)" "system…
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot and fix an import error issue when it shows "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device"
incidents.solution: When FortiManager import policy package from FortiGate shows fails as following:The Download Import Report shows as following:"system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-IP-BlockList1, oid=2634, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)" "system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-BlockURL_IP_Group1, oid=2636, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)"What happened is FortiManager being unable to copy the password from system external-resource due to it being encrypted.To solve the issue, disable the "private-data-encrytion" in Device Manager -> Device & Groups -> select the FortiGate -> CLI Configurations -> System -> Global.After changing the setting, FortiManager's Import Configuration does not fail anymore

incidents.title: FortiGate 201G upgrade from FortiOS version 8.0.1 to FortiOS version 8.0.2 fails during reboot
incidents.summary: DescriptionUpgrading a FortiGate 201G from FortiOS 8.0.1 to 8.0.2 via the GUI may cause the reboot process to stall and fail.ScopeFortiGate 201G, FortiOS version 8.0.1.SolutionWhen performing a firmware upgrade from FortiOS version 8.0.1 to version 8.0.2 on a FortiGate 201G using the GUI, the system initiates the reboot process but fails to complete it. The process is stuck at the 'Rebooting new firmware' stage and does not finish.Console prints the console prints 'Image verification OK!' followed by 'Failed to get the image encryption key!'.

incidents.title: Copilot is not usable after an upgrade to version 7.6.8 while the Explicit Proxy is in use
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to version 7.6.8, when using the FortiGate as an Explicit Proxy with the default settings, chat messages for Copilot will be blocked.ScopeFortiOS version 7.6.8+.SolutionAfter upgrading to version 7.6.8, users who are trying to talk to Copilot may see the following message appear:This is similar behaviour to what would occur on versions 7.6.6 and 7.6.7 due to a known issue in those versions tracked under 1308272 and 1257499.
incidents.symptom: After upgrading to version 7.6.8, when using the FortiGate as an Explicit Proxy with the default settings, chat messages for Copilot will be blocked
incidents.solution: After upgrading to version 7.6.8, users who are trying to talk to Copilot may see the following message appear:This is similar behaviour to what would occur on versions 7.6.6 and 7.6.7 due to a known issue in those versions tracked under 1308272 and 1257499. If on these versions, refer to this article instead:Troubleshooting Tip: Resolving Microsoft Copilot access issues with FortiGate inspecting traffic with a policy in proxy-mode and Application Control/IPS.If being on version 7.6.8 and have this issue, check the Forward Traffic logs filtered to the user's source IP. The following log may be visible:The traffic is being allowed by UTM, but denied by the proxy due to 'traffic denied because uri too long'. The maximum length of a request for an Explicit Proxy is defined by 'max-request-length', and this message will be seen when the proxy blocks the request due to exceeding this limit.The following commands can be used to change this limit:config web-proxy profile set max-request-length 64 endOnce this value is changed to the maximum, the traffic is allowed

incidents.title: LDAPS authentication fails due to an incorrect member-attr configuration
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to resolve an issue when users fail to authenticate via LDAPS because the member-attr is incorrectly set to tokenGroups, preventing the FortiGate from matching users to their assigned groups.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionUsers cannot authenticate via LDAPS even though the LDAP server returns a success response. The authentication fails during the group matching phase.The FortiGate is configured to use the tokenGroups attribute to retrieve group memberships.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to resolve an issue when users fail to authenticate via LDAPS because the member-attr is incorrectly set to tokenGroups, preventing the FortiGate from matching users to their assigned groups
incidents.solution: Users cannot authenticate via LDAPS even though the LDAP server returns a success response. The authentication fails during the group matching phase.The FortiGate is configured to use the tokenGroups attribute to retrieve group memberships. If the Active Directory environment does not populate this attribute or if it is not the correct attribute for the environment, the FortiGate finds zero values and skips group matching, resulting in an authentication failure for the user.Verify the issue via debug:Run the following commands to analyze the authentication process:diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug application fnbamd -1 diagnose debug enableLook for the following indicators in the debug output:attr='tokenGroups' - found 0 values: This indicates the FortiGate is looking for group memberships in the tokenGroups attribute but finding none.find_matched_usr_grps-Skipped group matching: This confirms that because no attributes were found, the user cannot be matched to any group.Correct the member-attr configuration:If tokenGroups is not required by the Active Directory configuration, revert the attribute to the default memberOf.Enter the CLI and navigate to the LDAP s

incidents.title: Administrator SSO authentication fails after upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.8.SolutionAfter upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential.The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login…
incidents.symptom: After upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account
incidents.solution: After upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential.The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login for FortiGate administrators with Entra ID acting as SAML IdP.Security Fabric SSO with root FortiGate as IdP, for example see Configuring single-sign-on in the Security Fabric.Confirmed not affected:VPN user SSO authentication.Other FortiOS versions including FortiOS 7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2.Local administrator authentication.Remote administrator authentication using RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+.While access to the FortiGate from FortiManagement Cloud (FortiGate Cloud) is technically not affected, SSO authentication to the FortiGate is still not possible over this management path.Issue matching:To confirm the issue, check the FortiOS crashlog for a matching "FORTISM Violation" from the time of the access attempt. This can be done by accessing the FortiGate using a local administrator account and executing diagnose debug crashlog read | gr Contournement : At this time, the only available workaround is to use another administrator authentication method.If no suitable administrator account exists, console access to a physical device can be used to recover access, see Technical Tip: Boot the backup firmware and config via console.If the device is centrally managed by FortiManager or a valid FortiManagement Cloud subscription, an administrator can be added. See Recover access to FortiGate via FortiManagement Cloud.Related article:Technical Tip: Create a 'break glass' admin account on the FortiGate as a backup for remote authentication/MFA (Recommendation)

incidents.title: FortiGate 30/31G Platform unable to upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8 "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification."
incidents.summary: DescriptionInstructions to resolve the "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification." error when upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8.ScopeFortiOS.SolutionWhen upgrading from FortiOS 7.6.7 to 7.6.8, you may face an error stating "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification." when the image has finished downloading (or uploading, if you are using the file upload function):This is a known issue with the 30/31G platform, and the solution is to upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.7 STS build 8767 before proceeding.
incidents.symptom: Instructions to resolve the "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification." error when upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.solution: When upgrading from FortiOS 7.6.7 to 7.6.8, you may face an error stating "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification." when the image has finished downloading (or uploading, if you are using the file upload function):This is a known issue with the 30/31G platform, and the solution is to upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.7 STS build 8767 before proceeding. To get this build, open a TAC ticket. After upgrading to this build, it will be possible to upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8 GA: FortiOS 7.6.7 GA -> 7.6.7 STS build8767 -> 7.6.8 GA

aiReview.summary: Problème lors de la mise à niveau de la plateforme FortiGate 30/31G vers FortiOS 7.6.8 avec une erreur de vérification de signature.
aiReview.symptom: Apparition du message d'erreur "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification." lors du téléchargement ou du chargement de l'image de mise à niveau vers FortiOS 7.6.8.
aiReview.solution: Il s'agit d'un problème connu sur la plateforme 30/31G. La solution consiste à effectuer la mise à niveau vers FortiOS 7.6.7 STS build 8767 (obtenue via un ticket TAC) avant de procéder à la mise à niveau vers FortiOS 7.6.8 GA.
